Beyond Statistical Fitting: Next-Generation Science-Informed Neural Architectures

Partha Pratim Ray
Sikkim University, India

Dominant AI architectures—Transformers, CNNs, GNNs, and Diffusion models—treat physical reality as unconstrained statistical correlation over discrete tensors. Bridging the gap to scientific discovery and resilient autonomy requires 12 next-generation neural models that hard-wire physical conservation, quantum chemistry, biological agency, and unified multi-domain laws directly into their computational fabric.

Core thesis: Adding soft physics or biology loss penalties to black-box networks is only a transitional step. True scientific and futuristic AI shifts from data-fitted weights to law-embedded, geometry-native, and thermodynamically self-organizing substrates—culminating in All-Informed neural engines that couple quantum chemistry, continuum physics, and living-system adaptation across scales.

Legacy paradigms audited for structural ceilings
12
Proposed futuristic models across 4 scientific pillars

Unconstrained Neural Architectures Fail When Laws, Scales, or Causality Shift

Modern deep learning excels at interpolation within dense training distributions, yet every major architecture hits predictable mathematical and physical walls once deployed in scientific, multi-scale, or open-ended environments. Even first-generation Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) inherit optimization pathologies from standard multilayer perceptrons because physical equations are merely added as competing soft penalty terms in the loss function.

Existing Paradigm Core Structural Limitations Scientific & Futuristic Bottleneck
Transformers Self-attention scales quadratically with sequence length (O(N²)), weights remain static after training, and next-token objectives lack built-in conservation or causal invariance (InterviewNode, 2026; Hugging Face Papers). Prohibitive energy cost on long multi-scale trajectories; plausible hallucinations that violate mass, energy, or chemical stoichiometry out of distribution.
CNNs Locked to rigid Euclidean grids and local receptive fields; translation equivariance breaks under 3D rotation, curvature, or irregular meshes (PMC, 2025). Cannot natively represent deformable biological tissues, non-Euclidean manifolds, or irregular molecular topologies without heavy discretization loss.
RNNs & SSMs (Mamba/S4) Compress all history into a fixed-size hidden state; while linear-time Mamba-2 improves long-sequence throughput, fixed-state bottlenecks degrade exact associative recall and sharp regime transitions. Struggle with multi-body spatial interactions and stiff multi-timescale dynamics where microsecond reactions steer macroscopic outcomes.
Graph Neural Networks (MPNNs) Repeated local message passing triggers oversmoothing (node features collapse) and oversquashing (long-range signals choke through bottlenecks), bounded by Weisfeiler-Leman expressivity (arXiv:2608.16097, 2026). Fail on non-local quantum effects in conjugated molecules and cannot directly encode 3-body or higher-order ring/complex interactions.
Diffusion Models Require tens to hundreds of iterative denoising steps; standard reverse-time score matching does not enforce exact conservation laws or thermodynamic dissipation bounds (arXiv:2601.06071, 2025). Slow sampling and physically invalid intermediate states during molecular conformation, fluid, or material generation.
1st-Gen PINNs Suffer from spectral bias (slow convergence on high-frequency modes), stiff multi-term loss landscapes, temporal causality violations, and single-geometry retraining (arXiv:2602.19265, 2026; arXiv:2606.25151, 2026). Silent failures on turbulent, chaotic, or shock-dominated systems; cannot amortize across new boundary geometries without operator learning.

Moving From Soft Loss Penalties to Hard-Wired Invariances Unlocks Extrapolation

Current scientific AI research is crossing a structural divide. First-generation domain-informed models bolted differential equations onto standard MLPs as soft regularizers. Emerging architectures—including Physics-Informed Neural Operators (PINOs), Equivariant GNNs, and Port-Metriplectic Neural Networks—embed symmetries, function-space mappings, and thermodynamic brackets directly into the network layers. The next frontier unifies these hard invariants across physics, chemistry, and biology.

Physics-Informed Models Must Evolve From PDE Solvers Into Relativistic and Thermodynamic Engines

First-generation PINNs solve one boundary-value problem at a time and struggle with chaotic or dissipative physics. Recent advances—including Neural Operators, Stable Port-Hamiltonian Neural Networks, Copresheaf Topological Neural Networks, and Thermodynamic Computing—point toward three genuinely new physics-native neural architectures.

Model 01 · Physics + Topology

Gauge-Covariant Sheaf Neural Operators (GCSNO)

Fuses equivariant bundle/sheaf theory with function-space neural operators. Instead of solving PDEs on flat Cartesian grids, GCSNO attaches local vector spaces (stalks) to curved, dynamic meshes and enforces exact local gauge covariance—opening zero-shot simulation for fusion plasma confinement, deformable metamaterials, and relativistic astrophysics.

Model 02 · Physics + Hardware

Metriplectic Thermodynamic Diffusion Networks (MTDN)

Combines Port-Metriplectic formalism (guaranteeing energy conservation via symplectic brackets and non-negative entropy via metric brackets) with physical thermodynamic computing. Rather than simulating noise on power-hungry GPUs, the hardware's native thermal fluctuations execute physically consistent generative sampling at a fraction of digital energy limits.

Model 03 · Physics + Continuous Adaptation

Noether-Symmetry Self-Discovering Liquid Networks (NS-LNN)

Extends continuous-time Liquid Neural Networks with differentiable Lie-group symmetry discovery layers inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold symbolic splines. As the network streams live telemetry from unknown physical environments (deep-space probes, hypersonic flight, autonomous underwater robotics), it infers hidden continuous symmetries and locks corresponding conservation laws into hard architectural constraints in real time.

Chemistry-Informed Networks Need Quantum-Electronic and Reaction-Pathway Priors

Standard molecular GNNs treat molecules as flat ball-and-stick graphs, losing electron delocalization, spin states, and multi-atom transition geometries. While E(3)-Equivariant GNNs, Green's-function neural networks, and Equivariant Matrix Function Networks have begun capturing non-local electronic effects, futuristic chemical discovery demands architectures built directly on fermionic wavefunctions, higher-order complexes, and interfacial electrochemistry.

Model 04 · Quantum Chemistry

Fermionic Equivariant Tensor-Field Networks (FETFN)

Hard-wires Pauli exclusion, wavefunction antisymmetry, and spin-orbit coupling into equivariant tensor-field layers. Unlike empirical force fields that fail during bond breaking, FETFN targets non-local electron correlation and excited-state photochemistry—enabling inverse design of room-temperature catalysts, quantum emitters, and next-generation photovoltaics.

Model 05 · Topological Chemistry

Higher-Order Simplicial Reaction-Pathway Networks (HSRPN)

Replaces pairwise message passing with topological simplicial and cell complexes where 2-cells represent aromatic rings and 3-cells encode coordinated transition states, paired with Green's-function non-local propagators. Eliminates GNN oversquashing to predict multi-step catalytic synthesis and non-equilibrium reaction networks.

Model 06 · Interfacial Materials

Electrochemical Phase-Boundary Neural Operators (EPBNO)

Couples atomistic quantum charge-transfer priors with continuum ion-transport neural operators across moving solid-liquid interfaces. Designed to bridge 9 orders of magnitude in length and time for self-healing solid-state battery interphases, direct-air carbon capture sorbents, and electrochemical nitrogen fixation.

Biology-Informed AI Shifts From Static Backpropagation to Self-Organizing, Active-Inference Agency

Living intelligence operates with ~20 watts of power, learns continuously without catastrophic forgetting, and regenerates after physical damage—capabilities completely absent from static backpropagation networks. Emerging work in Biology-Informed Neural Networks (BINNs), Predictive Coding with Spiking Neural Networks, Brain-Inspired Neural Cellular Automata (BraiNCA), and Active Inference cognitive robotics unlocks three radically new biological paradigms.

Model 07 · Morphogenetic AI

Morphogenetic Bioelectric Cellular Networks (MBCN)

Extends morphogenetic Neural Cellular Automata with simulated bioelectric voltage-gradient signaling and multiscale competency. Instead of fixed layer topologies, MBCN cells grow their own neural wiring, coordinate decentralized goal-directed behavior, and autonomously self-repair damaged sub-networks in soft robotics and resilient edge swarms.

Model 08 · Neuromorphic Agency

Homeostatic Predictive-Coding Spiking Fabrics (HPCSF)

Eliminates global backpropagation in favor of strictly local, event-driven spike-timing plasticity and hierarchical prediction-error minimization grounded in the Free Energy Principle, governed by explicit metabolic energy budgets. Built for hybrid memristor neuromorphic arrays to enable lifelong, ultra-low-power adaptation.

Model 09 · Systems Biology

Multi-Omic Causal-Pathway Graph Transformers (MOCGT)

Constrains sparse attention and message routing directly onto curated gene-regulatory, signaling, and metabolic pathways—building on BINN robustness against spurious correlations. Enables interpretable whole-cell perturbation prediction from genome to phenotype for personalized regenerative medicine.

“Living matter does not separate hardware, software, and objective function; it computes through self-regulating local competencies that minimize surprise under strict thermodynamic budgets.”
Architectural takeaway synthesized from morphogenetic NCA and Free Energy Principle robotics research (2024–2026)

All-Informed Architectures Fuse Physics, Chemistry, and Biology Into One Multi-Scale Engine

Real-world grand challenges—a living cell, a photosynthetic bioreactor, a synthetic organ, or Earth's coupled climate-biosphere—never obey physics, chemistry, or biology in isolation. While early Physics Foundation Models and Scientific Foundation Models pretrain across multiple PDEs or sequences, they still lack a shared mathematical grammar linking quantum bonding, continuum mechanics, and biological agency. Three proposed All-Informed (Omni-Science) architectures directly close this gap.

Model 10 · All-Informed Modular

Universal Port-Coupled Scientific Foundation Models (UP-SFM)

Generalizes Port-Metriplectic coupling across disciplines into a compositional "network of networks." Quantum-chemical equivariant modules, continuum PDE operators, and biological pathway networks exchange state exclusively through conserved energy, momentum, and mass-flux ports—guaranteeing physical consistency across full digital twins of cells, bioreactors, or planetary ecosystems.

Model 11 · All-Informed Unified Math

Topo-Thermodynamic Active Inference Networks (TT-AIN)

Unifies Topological Deep Learning (sheaves over multi-scale complexes), non-equilibrium thermodynamics (entropy-production bounds), and biological Active Inference (variational free-energy minimization) under one mathematical objective—treating physical stability, chemical equilibrium, and biological goal-seeking as regimes of a single free-energy geometry.

Model 12 · All-Informed Substrate

Symbiotic Wetware–Photonic Hybrid Networks (SWPHN)

A post-silicon physical neural architecture pairing photonic wave-interference layers (solving linear wave physics at the speed of light), chemically gated ionic/memristive synapses (encoding multi-timescale kinetics), and living biological cellular/organoid assemblies (providing self-repairing adaptive plasticity) inside one closed-loop computing substrate.

Feasibility Spans Near-Term Operator Hybrids to Decade-Scale Physical Substrates

Not all 12 proposals require new hardware. Software-native architectures built on equivariant operators, simplicial complexes, and causal biological wiring can be prototyped on current GPU clusters immediately, whereas thermodynamic and bio-hybrid substrates require co-designing mathematics alongside novel silicon, photonic, or biological hardware.

Horizon Candidate Models Primary Engineering Bottleneck to Solve
Near-Term (1–3 yr) HSRPN, MOCGT, EPBNO, GCSNO Building fast GPU kernels for higher-order simplicial/sheaf operations and curating coupled multi-scale scientific benchmarks.
Mid-Term (3–7 yr) FETFN, NS-LNN, HPCSF, UP-SFM, TT-AIN Scaling antisymmetric fermionic layers without cubic bottlenecks, stabilizing online symmetry discovery, and standardizing cross-domain energy-flux port interfaces.
Moonshot (7–15+ yr) MTDN, MBCN (physical), SWPHN Fabricating programmable thermodynamic/memristor chips, maintaining long-term wetware-photonic biocompatibility, and formalizing verification for self-modifying substrates.
